value.name: Marylin reports Miles's invitation
value.description: Marylin tells her friends that Miles said to make the house hers.
evidence: MARYLIN (Sigh) Well. He said to "make the house mine."

value.name: friends react to Miles's naivete
value.description: Ramona responds skeptically to Marylin's report, implying Miles does not understand what he is saying.
evidence: RAMONA Oh boy. If he only knew.

value.name: Marylin admits Miles is unexpected
value.description: Marylin says Miles is not what she expected and describes him as unusually happy.
evidence: MARYLIN He's not what I expected. He's very -- he's so -- happy.

value.name: Marylin confirms marriage plans
value.description: When asked, Marylin confirms that she is still going through with the marriage.
evidence: SARAH But you're going through with it?

value.name: Marylin reflects on being a second wife
value.description: Marylin explains that she has never been the first wife and notes that Rex was married before her.
evidence: you know I've never been the first wife. Rex was married before me.

value.name: Marylin contrasts Miles with Rex
value.description: Marylin says Miles is different from her previous husband because he remains idealistic.
evidence: MARYLIN Miles is different. He's still so idealistic.

value.name: Sarah predicts Miles will change
value.description: Sarah warns Marylin that Miles's idealism will soon be replaced by cynicism.
evidence: SARAH Well, that's about to change big time.

value.name: Marylin notes absence of rage
value.description: Marylin observes that Miles has no cynicism or anger and that she is no longer absorbing rage directed at another woman.
evidence: He has no cynicism or anger. For once I'm not the repository of rage at some other woman.

value.name: Sarah jokes about future rage
value.description: Sarah jokes that Marylin will soon have her own rage, and Marylin half-accepts the remark.
evidence: SARAH Soon, you'll have your own rage!
